programme: HOXA1 and SOX17 (HOXA1's own target list includes SOX17) form a Müllerian-epithelium patterning axis, gated by the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler ARID1A, which controls access to differentiation and cell-cycle targets (CCND1, MYC, PCNA, CDH1, SMAD3) that define endometrioid glandular identity.
role_in_a: In endometrioid/Müllerian carcinoma, SOX17 and HOXA1 mark and drive glandular/mesonephric-like differentiation (SOX17 percentile 0.94 in Endometrioid_Cancer, 3 diagnostic-pathology PMIDs; HOXA1 promotes proliferation via the HOTAIRM1/HOXA1 axis), while ARID1A loss-of-function is one of the defining tumor-suppressor lesions of this histology (percentile 0.97, 4 PMIDs on SWI/SNF-deficient endometrioid/ovarian carcinoma), de-repressing the same programme to permit uncontrolled growth.
role_in_b: No retrieved evidence places this programme in adult stroke pathophysiology (ischemia, thrombosis, atherosclerosis, neuroinflammation). What is documented for two of the three factors in a vascular/cardiac context is developmental rather than disease-mechanistic: HOXA1 loss-of-function causes a congenital vascular malformation syndrome (carotid artery anomalies, PMID 39541495 'HOXA1-Related Disorders'; heart malformation in a zebrafish model, PMID 37508332), and ARID1A gates cardiomyocyte proliferation during heart maturation (PMID 37543677) — organogenesis roles, not stroke risk factors.
shared_axis: If this HOXA1/SOX17/ARID1A module is simply the same organogenesis toolkit redeployed in two tissues — Müllerian epithelium in one case, carotid/cardiac vasculature in the other — then its presence in both disease groups reflects developmental reuse of a chromatin-gated patterning circuit, not a stroke mechanism. The one hit that gestures toward an actual clinical bridge (PMID 33758607, concerning both diseases) discusses venous thromboembolism and cerebrovascular events as a general complication of ovarian/endometrioid-family carcinomas, i.e. a paraneoplastic hypercoagulability route that these specific factors are not shown to drive.
reasoning: The module is coherent and strongly anchored in disease A (8 direct endometrioid/Müllerian-carcinoma PMIDs spanning all three carrying factors, both at high Open Targets percentiles), which rules out 'incoherent'. But nothing retrieved documents this programme's involvement in stroke biology proper — only unrelated developmental/cardiovascular papers for HOXA1 and ARID1A — so the cross-disease bridge is inference about tissue-patterning reuse rather than retrieved joint evidence, which caps this below 'supported'.
support: 41808247, 39245863, 41664069 — place SOX17 in endometrioid/Müllerian carcinoma diagnosis; 42199023, 42162929, 41510478, 42274628 — place ARID1A/SWI-SNF loss in endometrioid and related ovarian carcinoma; 31853186 — HOTAIRM1/HOXA1 axis promotes endometrial cancer proliferation and invasion; 39541495 — HOXA1-related disorders include vascular (carotid) malformation; 37508332 — HOXA1 loss causes heart malformation in a zebrafish model; 37543677 — ARID1A-mediated YAP inhibition governs cardiomyocyte proliferation during heart maturation; 33758607 — concerns both diseases, discussing VTE/cerebrovascular events as a complication of ovarian/endometrioid-family carcinoma.
how_to_falsify: Compare stroke incidence and thrombotic markers (D-dimer, tissue factor) between ARID1A-deficient and ARID1A-intact endometrioid tumors in a matched cohort; separately, check HOXA1 and SOX17 expression/chromatin activity in adult cerebrovascular endothelium or stroke thrombectomy specimens (ChIP-seq/RNA-seq) — if neither factor is active there, the stroke-side hits are purely developmental/incidental and the shared-module account is refuted.
caveats: 36 patient-group comparisons across only 4 independent cohort pairs, and the tissue pairing (blood vs uterine endometrium) is not anatomically adjacent, so any cross-disease claim is weaker than the raw comparison count suggests. MEF2D was excluded despite recurring in 15/36 comparisons and having real stroke literature (33621420, 32311345) because it is explicitly discordant, not concordant, between the two diseases. The single-view exclusions (HOXA13, NANOG, POU2F3, etc.) show no single subgroup is driving this account. The tissue-generic exclusions (CREB5, BCL6, STAT1, SPI1, IRF1, and others) removed the immune/hematopoietic master regulators that would otherwise be the obvious explanation for the blood side — their absence is why this account reaches for a developmental module instead of an immune one, not an oversight. GTF3A, DMTF1, E2F8, and TFAP4 carry no literature support in either disease and are excluded entirely.
